subject: Dedicated pool: procurement cadence, OEM ETAs & cloud fill options
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos@omega-oem.com>, Emma Li <emma@auroracloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated pool: procurement cadence, OEM ETAs & cloud fill options

Hi Carlos / Emma,

We're aligning the timeline for the AcmeAI dedicated capacity commitment (DEAL-8472). The commercial team has signaled a target onramp window that begins mid-Q2 2027, but we need to lock a procurement cadence to avoid surprises on lead times and customs hold-ups.

Can you each fill the attached ETA_request_template.xlsx with:
- realistic ship windows for the relevant SKUs (best-case / typical / worst-case)
- earliest acceptance-test window for each tranche
- any export/customs or depot staging constraints (region-specific)
- firm holdbacks or minimum order quantities that would change ETA

Carlos: please include OEM quote reference numbers and any scheduling buffers you recommend.
Emma: please outline Aurora Cloud reserved capacity options (short-term reserved or burst) that we can use as a backfill if hardware slips. We need estimated provisioning lead (in weeks) and any cost delta.

Goal: consolidate a matrix by Nov 30 so we can decide split between OEM direct procurement and cloud-reserved backfill, and schedule the PO trigger (we prefer a two-phased PO: deposit + final).

Thanks —
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ETA_request_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@omega-oem.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Raj Patel <raj@omega-oem.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: procurement cadence, OEM ETAs & cloud fill options

Naomi, team,

Thanks for the request — see attached for our initial ETA and quote package (omega_quote_20261123.pdf). High-level summary here:

- SKUs: OMEGA-A100X / OMEGA-HX2 (quantization-friendly variant)
- Best-case ship window after PO (availability from our US depot): 10–12 weeks
- Typical ship window: 12–16 weeks
- Worst-case: 18–22 weeks (if component shortage or QA rework)
- Acceptance testing: we can offer a 5–7 day site-acceptance test window after unit-level burn-in and network integration (we recommend scheduling a 2-week rolling acceptance per tranche)
- Minimum order per tranche: 8 GPUs (we can split into 8/8/whatever but lead time improves with larger consolidated orders)
- Customs/transport: east coast ports are faster for our shipments (NY/NJ) but note potential 7–14 day hold if CIF terms are used — we typically ship DDP to avoid surprises but that adds cost.

If you plan a multi-tranche order, we recommend staggering by at least 3–4 weeks to allow for parallel QA and avoid port congestion. We included two quote references in the PDF.

On cost: the attached quote includes a 3% early-commit discount if deposit is received within 14 days of quote acceptance.

Regards,
Carlos Mendez
Head of OEM Sales
Omega OEM
carlos@omega-oem.com

Attachments: omega_quote_20261123.pdf
From: Emma Li <emma@auroracloud.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: procurement cadence, OEM ETAs & cloud fill options

Hi Naomi,

Appreciate the heads-up. Aurora can provide two short-term programs to reduce customer risk while OEM gear ships:

1) Reserved Burst: reserved compute that can be stood up within ~2–4 weeks, billed as a committed tranche with an uplift (~18% delta vs our standard on-demand). Reserved burst is available in US-West and US-East regions.

2) Capacity Guarantee (short term): we can hold a soft-reserved pool for up to 12 weeks for a smaller fee (roughly 8% of month one committed spend) while hardware is in transit; this requires a short MSA amendment.

For either option we can provide a cost/benefit sketch for the expected token throughput. See attached Aurora offer. Note: our provisioning SLA is 99.9% for reserved capacity; provisioning lead is dependent on the SKU mix you need (GPUs with NVLink might add 1 extra week).

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through tradeoffs — available Thursday morning PST.

Best,
Emma Li
Strategic Cloud Partnerships
Aurora Cloud
emma@auroracloud.com

Attachments: aurora_reserved_offer.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: procurement cadence, OEM ETAs & cloud fill options

Thanks Carlos / Emma — good context. Quick internal summary and proposed approach:

- Sizing: AcmeAI committed: 128 x accelerator-equivalent GPUs (effective for our scheduler); recommend breaking into 3 tranches: 48 / 48 / 32 to allow earlier capacity on customer-critical lanes.
- OEM plan: place tranche 1 PO immediately for 48 units (target ship 12–14 weeks per Omega quote). Tranche 2 PO to follow on formal contract milestone (expected +4–6 weeks).
- Cloud fill: provision Aurora Reserved Burst for first 8–10 weeks to cover customer ramp. This buys time for OEM acceptance and reduces outage risk.
- Acceptance windows: request 2-week rolling acceptance per tranche; schedule preliminary SAT (site acceptance test) calendar now.
- Customs & staging: route for DDP shipments to NY depot to minimize port holds; budget 10 business days staging buffer.

Action items:
1) Naomi: confirm PO trigger dates and whether Acme wants deposit schedule (we should align with 3% early-commit discount Carlos mentioned).
2) Ben: draft SAT calendar and ops handoff checklist for tranche 1 (include test harness and expected KV cache warm-up targets).
3) Lauren: coordinate procurement approval timeline and check finance for deposit vs milestone release.

I've attached a quick provisioning schedule (provisioning_schedule_v1.csv) — it's preliminary.

-Karthik
Group Product Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: provisioning_schedule_v1.csv
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: procurement cadence, OEM ETAs & cloud fill options

Team,

Thanks for the quick turn. Per internal alignment and the attachments:

Decisions:
- We will proceed with the OEM path for the bulk of capacity and use Aurora Reserved Burst to cover the initial customer ramp.
- PO cadence: Tranche 1 PO (48 units) to be issued by Redwood procurement on Dec 08 to trigger the 3% early-commit discount; target invoice deposit to be 25% of tranche value.
- SAT/Acceptance: schedule two-week rolling SATs starting the estimated week of arrival per Omega; Ben, please publish the SAT calendar by Dec 03.

Requests for vendors:
- Carlos: confirm DDP vs CIF pricing in the final quote and confirm earliest ship optimism (we will commit Dec 08 if the 3% discount stays). Please send a redline that clarifies customs responsibilities.
- Emma: provision the Reserved Burst estimate and hold a soft pool through Mar 31, 2027 (Aurora — can you confirm the short hold fee and exact SKU match so Finance can reconcile?)

Links & artifacts: HubSpot deal https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/DEAL-8472 — I'll attach the PO checklist and route the DocuSign when procurement has the final quote.

Next steps:
- Dec 03: Ben publishes SAT calendar & ops checklist.
- Dec 04: Finance to confirm deposit release process.
- Dec 08: Procurement issues tranche 1 PO contingent on confirmed DDP pricing and final quote.

Please reply only if you see a blocker on your side by EOD Dec 04.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Attachments: acme_po_trigger_checklist.pdf
